name: The Totem of Infliction
summary: In Darkshire, Madame Eva offers travelers a ward against Duskwood's dangers. She needs ghoul fangs, skeleton fingers, and spider venom to enchant the Totem of Infliction, a charm that strikes back at attackers.

sections.title: A Fortune of Bloodshed
sections.body: Madame Eva reads the fortunes of those who enter her candle-lit home in Darkshire. She senses danger and violence ahead, then offers practical sorcery alongside her divinations. To make a ward against Duskwood's predators, she needs ten ghoul fangs, ten skeleton fingers, and five vials of spider venom gathered from the haunted woods.

sections.title: Eva's Enchantment
sections.body: Madame Eva binds ghoul fangs, fingers from restless skeletons, and spider venom with enchantments. In mortal peril, the totem gives off a magical aura that reflects cruelty, harming anyone who strikes its bearer.

faq.answer: Madame Eva is a fortune teller and mystic who lives in Darkshire. She reads omens and makes protective wards for locals and travelers facing Duskwood's supernatural dangers.

faq.q: What is the purpose of the Totem of Infliction?
faq.answer: The Totem of Infliction is an enchanted charm meant to ward off attackers. When its bearer is threatened, its magic strikes back at those who try to harm them.

faq.q: Why does Madame Eva need ghoul fangs, skeleton fingers, and spider venom?
faq.answer: Madame Eva uses ghoul fangs, skeleton fingers, and spider venom to make a protective enchantment that retaliates against attackers.

faq.q: Where are the components for the totem found?
faq.answer: The components come from undead and beasts in Duskwood. Ghouls and skeletons haunt its cemeteries and orchards, while large venomous spiders live throughout the shadowed woods.

faq.q: What danger does Madame Eva foresee?
faq.answer: Madame Eva warns of danger and bloodshed ahead. She says whispering winds speak of a threat on the traveler's path.

faq.q: Is crafting the totem considered dark magic?
faq.answer: Eva's work draws on grim folk sorcery and corpse parts, but Duskwood's dangers make protective charms an accepted means of defense.

angles.text: Alliance travelers in a borderland cut off from major military reinforcements often rely on local mystics like Madame Eva for folk charms and wards.
As a paladin, you may question making a ward from undead bones and spider venom. Duskwood's dangers can make practical folk sorcery hard to dismiss.
As a warlock, you recognize the retaliatory curses woven into Eva's protective charm.
As a priest, you know the Church of the Holy Light teaches faith and devotion, while mystics like Madame Eva channel spiritual will through grim, tangible charms.
